items.title: Negotiations finalised to link EU and UK Emissions Trading Systems
items.summary: EU and UK leaders announced at a bilateral summit that negotiations on linking their Emissions Trading Systems are concluded; the link is to apply from 1 January 2028, subject to ratification. The UK will extend its ETS to aviation and maritime, and the agreement could provide the basis for a future mutual exemption from each side's CBAM.
items.why_it_matters: A common carbon price across the North Sea changes the economics of UK–EU CO2 flows; Carbon Management Europe notes cross-border storage recognition for ETS compliance is still not envisaged before 2031.

items.title: Longer project duration leads to higher Porthos project budget
items.summary: Porthos says construction will be completed by the end of 2027 at the earliest, with operations realistically starting in 2028; delays centre on the offshore platform and the compressor station. The cost increase is estimated at up to €397 million including a risk buffer, raising the budget from the €1.3 billion FID baseline to a maximum of €1.7 billion.
items.why_it_matters: Hard cost-overrun and schedule data for a pipeline-based North Sea transport and storage system, useful for calibrating capex and start-up uncertainty in network models.

items.title: publication 20/11/2026 Joint letter calling for an IPCEI on Industrial Carbon Management On 20 November 2026, Carbon Management Europe joined 25 other… Open Letters Read More
items.summary: Carbon Management Europe and 25 other organisations ask Member States to launch a JEF-IPCEI identification process for a combined CCUS programme, name lead coordinating bodies and commission a scoping study. They want the 2024 Industrial Carbon Management Strategy turned into a co-investment programme linking capture, cross-border transport, utilisation and storage, with design work starting in 2027.
items.why_it_matters: An IPCEI would be a new state-aid route for cross-border CO2 transport and storage chains, affecting how Nordic hubs and shipping links could be financed.

items.title: Techno-economic evaluation report
items.summary: Bottom-up techno-economic assessment of full CCS chains in four European regions, including the Baltic Sea and the North Sea, comparing direct ship injection (DSI) with a dedicated pipeline and with conventional shipping to an offshore platform (net present costs in 2030 euros, 2031–2065). Capture accounts for roughly 65–90% of full-chain costs; pipelines give the lowest transport and storage cost where feasible, while DSI and conventional shipping have similar costs.
items.why_it_matters: Directly comparable mode-choice cost data (pipeline vs ship vs direct injection) for the Baltic and North Sea, usable as input to Nordic-Baltic network optimisation.

items.title: Techno-economic drivers and challenges for direct ship injection including replicability analysis
items.summary: Assesses drivers, barriers and replicability of direct ship injection (DSI), where a CO2 carrier connects to a subsea injection system without an offshore platform or pipeline, for Portugal, the Baltic Sea, the Black Sea and the North Sea. DSI is found most useful in early deployment with low-to-medium volumes and dispersed emitters; main barriers are regulatory, operational and commercial, and in a Mediterranean network model DSI was not lowest-cost but appeared in several near-optimal routes.
items.why_it_matters: Clarifies when platform-free ship injection belongs in an optimal CO2 network, relevant to Baltic emitters without pipeline access and to Norwegian DSI projects such as Atlas.

items.summary: DG Energy explainer on industrial carbon management stating that the Commission plans to propose legislation for an internal CO2 market and infrastructure in early 2027, and recalling the NZIA target of 50 Mt/yr of storage capacity by 2030. It notes the latest PCI/PMI list includes 17 CO2 transport and storage projects, that CEF has given €978 million to CO2 infrastructure, and that Yara Sluiskil began capturing CO2 in September 2026 for shipment to Northern Lights.
items.why_it_matters: Confirms the timing of the EU CO2 market and infrastructure regulation, which will set access and tariff rules for cross-border pipeline and shipping networks.

items.title: UK building offshore carbon storage capability close to northern industrial clusters
items.summary: Feature by Jeremy Beckman on offshore storage projects: Endurance (East Coast Cluster, ~140 km offshore pipeline, Phase 1 injection above 5 Mt/yr), Morecambe Net Zero (pipeline from Peak Cluster cement and lime producers; a ship-based import concept at Barrow was studied), and Project Greensand, where CO2 is trucked to Esbjerg and shipped to Nini West. items.title: EnEarth to acquire Storegga's interest in Acorn to create one of Europe's largest CO2 transport and storage platforms
items.summary: Storegga has signed a sale and purchase agreement under which EnEarth, originally set up by Energean and now independent, will acquire Storegga's 30% working interest and Lead Developer status in the Acorn CCS project off northeast Scotland, subject to approvals, with completion expected by the end of 2026. Acorn holds Track-2 status in the UK cluster sequencing programme and covers the Acorn and East Mey storage licences (5-10 Mt/yr injection, over 140 Mt capacity). The enlarged EnEarth group also includes the Prinos storage project in Greece, the Devnya project in Bulgaria and Prime Marine, which brings CO2 shipping and direct offshore injection capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: Consolidates a North Sea storage developer with a CO2 shipping and direct-injection operator, a vertically integrated ship-plus-storage model relevant to how Nordic chains (Northern Lights, Greensand) compete for cross-border CO2 volumes.

items.title: Identifying and Structuring Risks in CCS Infrastructures - A Systematic Literature Review
items.summary: KIT working paper (Working Paper Series in Production and Energy, No. 84) reviewing 76 full-text publications on risks in large-scale CCS infrastructure linking capture, conditioning, transport and geological storage. The identified risks are mapped to five CCS stages and seven risk categories and consolidated into 35 risk clusters, presented as a risk matrix and a risk register with causes, impacts, mitigation measures and sources. The authors find that storage limitations, capacity shortfalls, technical interfaces and coordination problems often affect more than one stage, and note the tools do not replace quantitative risk assessment.
items.why_it_matters: A structured catalogue of cross-stage risks (capacity shortfalls, interfaces, coordination) that can be turned into uncertainty sets or scenarios for stochastic and robust CCS network-design models.
items.authors: Moritz Fierke, Sonja Rosenberg, Vincent Bäsler, Frank Schultmann
